subject: Computing
name: JHS 3 Computing
description: The JHS 3 Computing curriculum consolidates learners' knowledge in computer systems, productivity software, communication networks and computational thinking. It covers advanced concepts like next-generation computers, perceptual computing, cloud storage, advanced productivity tools, network security and artificial intelligence.

strands.title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTING
strands.description: Advanced computer components, technology in the community and health and safety.

subStrands.title: COMPONENTS OF COMPUTERS AND COMPUTER SYSTEMS
subStrands.description: Next-generation computers, perceptual computing and storage systems.

contentStandards.description: Identify parts of a Computer and Technology Tools

indicators.description: Discuss the trends in the next generation of computers

exemplars.description: Identify features expected to be seen in the next generation of computers.
Describe Google quantum computer (sycamore) and compare its processing power with other supercomputers (focus on processor).

indicators.description: Examine the concept of Perceptual Computing

exemplars.description: Discuss the features of Perceptual Computing.

indicators.description: Discuss the uses of Output devices such as Wearable Displays, E-Paper, E-Books, Kindle

exemplars.description: Describe Wearable Displays (e.g. Google Glass), E-Paper, E-Books (e.g. Kindle).

indicators.description: Describe Storage Systems: Network and Cloud Storage Systems, Smart Cards, Holographic Storage, Storage Systems for Large Computer Systems (home servers or media servers)

exemplars.description: Discuss Network and Cloud Storage Systems, Smart Cards, Holographic Storage, Storage Systems for Large Computer Systems (home servers or media servers).
Explore common cloud storage examples such as Google Drive, One Drive, etc.
Discuss the pros and cons of using cloud storage.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the Use of the Desktop

indicators.description: Explore personalisation of the computer

exemplars.description: Change desktop icons.
Change mouse pointers.

indicators.description: Identify and use file management techniques (drivers and hardware)

exemplars.description: Identify and explore the use of device drivers e. g. sound drivers and video graphic drivers.
Explain plug-and-play devices.
Demonstrate how to install, update or delete drivers.

subStrands.title: TECHNOLOGY IN THE COMMUNITY (COMMUNICATION)
subStrands.description: Applying technology to solve community problems.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the Use of Technology in the Community

indicators.description: Evaluate problems in the community that can be solved with technology

exemplars.description: Discuss problems in the community that can be solved using technology Work in pairs.

indicators.description: Propose solutions to the problems identified

exemplars.description: Present technological solutions to the problems identified in B9.1.2.1.1.

indicators.description: Design the solution selected

exemplars.description: Design the solution selected.
Present the solution designed.

subStrands.title: HEALTH AND SAFETY IN THE USE OF ICT TOOLS
subStrands.description: Evaluating health and safety risks in ICT usage.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate How to Apply Health and Safety Measures in the Use ICT Tools

indicators.description: Evaluate health issues at workstations

exemplars.description: Discuss the use of ergonomic tools such as ergonomic keyboard and paper stand.
Demonstrate the appropriateness of the lighting system while working with the computer.

indicators.description: Evaluate Safety Risk Reduction at issues at workstations

exemplars.description: Discuss the heat generated by machines (e.g. computers, printers etc.) and how to reduce excess heat.

strands.title: PRODUCTIVITY SOFTWARE
strands.description: Advanced features in Word Processing, Presentation, Desktop Publishing and Spreadsheets.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate How to Use Microsoft Word (Multimedia)

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to add pictures, insert a screenshot and screen clipping and print screen

exemplars.description: Explore the use of the clip art, screenshot and screen clipping in the Insert Ribbon.
Demonstrate the use of the print screen key in capturing and inserting pictures.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the use of SmartArt

exemplars.description: Illustrate the use of SmartArt in the Illustrations group of the Insert Ribbon.

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to add Multimedia (audios, videos, animations), Charts and Hyperlinks

exemplars.description: Explore the use of the clip art and screenshot in the Insert Ribbon.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate How to use Microsoft PowerPoint (Multimedia)

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to add pictures and insert screenshots

exemplars.description: Explore the use of the clip art and screenshot in the Insert Ribbon.

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to animate slides in a presentation

exemplars.description: Demonstrate the use of transitions and animations.
Create a seven-slide presentation with animations and transitions.

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to add Multimedia (audios, videos etc.), tables and charts

exemplars.description: Explore the use of the Insert Ribbon tab to add multimedia (e.g. audios, videos, etc.).
Demonstrate the use of tables and charts in slides.

subStrands.title: INTRODUCTION TO DESKTOP PUBLISHING
subStrands.description: Creating and evaluating desktop published documents.

indicators.description: Create and present a desktop published document (flyer, advertisement, invitation cards, business cards)

exemplars.description: Create and present a four-page document with images and overflow e.g. flyer, advertisement, storybook.

indicators.description: Describe a desktop published document

exemplars.description: Give out your document to another learner assigned to you and collect the learner's document.
Examine the document received in terms of the position of text and images, use of colour, mechanics, content accuracy, etc.

indicators.description: Evaluate a desktop published document

exemplars.description: Evaluate the assigned document using, but not limited to the following criteria: position of text and images, general layout of the document, use of colour, mechanics (punctuation, spelling, italics, capitalisation, etc.), and appropriateness of the design for the intended purpose.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate How to Use Spreadsheet (Advanced Operations)

indicators.description: Perform data filtering, sorting and validation

exemplars.description: Describe Fields (columns), Records (rows) and Tables (structured/ unstructured).
Illustrate examples of structured and unstructured tables.
Construct a structured data table of class members (e.g. data table may have the following fields: Surname, First name, Date of Birth, Sex, Home Town, Region, etc).
Apply validation rules to check for errors.
Convert data tables to a list in MS Excel. Demonstrate the process of entering data to a list.
Demonstrate the use of validation list in the Sex column (in Exemplar(s): 3) to provide options in a drop-down for data entry.
Demonstrate how to sort data in alphabetical order (ascending/descending) and filter data to display only selected data.

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to use styles, themes, templates and macros

exemplars.description: Describe the difference between templates and macros.
Create new spreadsheet documents from predefined templates in MS Excel.
Demonstrate the use of styles and themes on sample worksheets.
Do a project on formatting a dataset by applying styles and themes.
Explore the use of macros.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the use of data tables, pivot tables, charts and pivot charts

exemplars.description: Explore pivot tables and charts.
Explore the use of a pivot table to display a summary of the dataset.
Insert a pivot chart to display the number of males and females in the class.
Demonstrate the use of the sort and filter features of the pivot table.

strands.title: COMMUNICATION NETWORKS
strands.description: Advanced networking concepts, social media risks, and security.

contentStandards.description: Know the Concept of Computer Networking for Global Communications

indicators.description: Discuss types of e-commerce and the cashless society (Bitcoin, Transaction cards, Quick Response code (QR) payment system)

exemplars.description: Explore the use of the Internet to engage in online business: selling, buying and paying for products online.
Discuss the use of online banking systems (e.g. using mobile money, bitcoin, the use of MasterCard, Visa card, QR code payment system, etc.).

indicators.description: Justify eLearning potentials

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of eLearning, its benefits and disadvantages.
Discuss projects on a collaborative platform (e.g. iBox network, the use of ad hoc network to share resources, Wikis, Google Docs] etc.)

subStrands.title: INTERNET AND SOCIAL MEDIA
subStrands.description: Social media risks and email features.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the Use of Social Networking and Electronic Mail

indicators.description: Identify the advantages and risks in the use of social media platforms

exemplars.description: Illustrate the benefits of using social media sites.
Discuss the issues and risks surrounding the usage of social media platforms and how to avoid them.
Explore reply, reply all, forward and forward all features in the use of emails.

contentStandards.description: Recognise data threats and the means of protection

indicators.description: Discuss cyberbullying, cyberstalking, digital footprint and digital shadow on the Internet

exemplars.description: Watch a film or do a reading on cyberbullying, cyberstalking, digital footprint, digital shadows.
Discuss the nature of cyberbullying, cyberstalking, digital footprint and digital shadows.
Identify examples of cyberbullying, cyberstalking, digital footprint and digital shadows.
Discuss the effects on cyberbullying on individuals.

indicators.description: Explain ten (10) information hacking techniques on the Internet environment

exemplars.description: Brainstorm information hacking techniques on the internet environment.
Explain ten (10) information hacking techniques e.g. phishing, keyloggers, Denial of Service attack, eavesdropping, etc.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the Use of a Web Browser (Blogging)

indicators.description: Examine the importance of creating blogs

exemplars.description: Discuss the importance of creating blogs.

indicators.description: Develop a blog for the school or a social club

exemplars.description: Investigate the items to include in a school or social club blog.
Develop a blog for the school or a social club.

indicators.description: Explore the steps in publishing a blog

exemplars.description: Identify steps in publishing a blog.
Demonstrate the procedure for publishing a blog and invite others to comment.

strands.title: COMPUTATIONAL THINKING
strands.description: Programming logic, algorithms, robotics, and artificial intelligence.

contentStandards.description: Show an Understanding of the Concept of Programming

indicators.description: Describe the conversion of decimal into binary data type for computer to recognise the meaning, process and store

exemplars.description: Convert decimal, binary and hexadecimal data from one format to another.
Show the results of calculating two or more binary numbers using the mathematical notation or operators in the number base two rule.

indicators.description: Identify the different tools which are accessible in Integrated Development Environment (IDE) to aid the development of codes

exemplars.description: Explore programming languages such as Snap, Scratch and Python to explain the key terminologies (variables, operators, controls, events, etc.) around the coding environment. Explore a web development programme to create a simple website.

subStrands.title: ALGORITHM
subStrands.description: Developing algorithms with flowcharts and pseudocode.

contentStandards.description: Analyse the Correct Step-by-step Procedure in Solving any Real-world Problem

indicators.description: Write a programme using flowchart and Pseudocode algorithm that includes sequence, selection and iteration choices in problem-solving

exemplars.description: Discuss at least three ways to do proper hand-washing and prepare beverages with or without sugar and/or milk.
Write an algorithm for Exemplar(s): 1 that focuses on procedure correctness and shortest time to execute.

indicators.description: Translate a Flowchart algorithm to Pseudocode format and vice versa

exemplars.description: Write an algorithm using flowchart format. Convert or translate the same flowchart algorithm into a Pseudocode format. (do a vice versa translation example to reinforce critical thinking)

indicators.description: Construct a robot artefact using available lab components and tools or emulator/simulator software pack

exemplars.description: Explain the three basic laws of robotics by Isaac Asimov i.e. Asimov's science fiction laws of robotics.
Demonstrate how a robot is assembled using real robots' toolkit/video/pictures.
Explore a robotic software pack, e.g. Scratch, Webot, Snap, Mbot software, EV3 and Mobile Applications such as lightbot

subStrands.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
subStrands.description: Expert systems and machine learning concepts.

indicators.description: Describe the knowledge-based systems (Expert systems) as the classical Artificial intelligence

exemplars.description: Illustrate the use of IF-THEN control structure for querying an expert system.
Demonstrate how to input a request in any knowledge-based system to generate an output or result (e.g. Telemedicine system).

Demonstrate how to go onto the web and use Google's Teachable Machine demo to get a basic understanding of how machine learning works (e.g. Whatisit as an open-source cloud-based app which can identify the object in an image/photo). NB: Demonstrate how data is collected and the extent to which information can be used. Also discuss thoughts on machine learning. https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com
